newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT HITS LOWEST POLL STANDING IN A YEAR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT HITS LOWEST POLL STANDING IN A YEAR.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's governing centre-right coalition has fallen to its lowest support level since elections last June, an opinion poll released on Wednesday showed.

The survey conducted by the state-run Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM) in early May put the coalition's support at 42.5 percent, down 1.5 percentage points from April and four points lower than in January.
Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) fell to only 18 percent from 23 percent in Febraury. Following the June vote, ODS had a 30 percent approval rating.

ODS's losses were made up somewhat by junior coalition member Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), which rose to its highest rating since the general election at 14.5 percent, while the third government party, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) dipped to 10 percent from a previous 11 percent.
The survey put the opposition Social Democrats at 25 percent, after 23 percent in April.
This is the first time ever an IVVM poll showed the CSSD pulling ahead of the ODS.

The survey was taken after the government announced a package of economic measures in mid-April aimed at restoration of economic growth and keeping fiscal balance through spending cuts and slowdown in wage growth.

"There can be a link to the package, the economists and enterpreneurs (who according to the poll largely left the ODS) reacted quite fast, and there also can be an expectations of a slowdown in the economic development," Eliska Rendlova, head of research at IVVM, told Reuters.
"It is caused by negative expectations concerning the near future, including fears of slower wage growth," she added.
Tensions have increased in the coalition since last June's parliamentary election at which it lost its majority.
And though it has since regained a majority through opposition defections, a downturn in the economy has prompted calls from many corners for wide-scale changes cabinet changes.

Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik is most-often mentioned for sacking after the state finances slipped into a deficit of 11.98 billion crowns for the year to April, and several investment funds -- which are regulated by his ministry -- were stripped of billions of crowns worth of assets.
Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy of ODA has also been under heavy fire, and Dlouhy himself has said recently that he may consider stepping down by the end of the year.
General elections are not due until mid-2000, but many analysts have said the government would likely fall before that time.
